script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for June 28. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You're huge compared to ants, tiny compared to mountains, microscopic compared to planets.  There is no absolute big or small—only comparison.  And at different scales, the rules change.

Double the size of something and surface area quadruples (2²) but volume goes up eight times (2³). This means larger creatures have proportionally less surface area. They can't cool as easily, can't support their weight as easily. Size brings constraints. Different forces dominate at different scales.  At tiny scales, surface tension rules—insects walk on water.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Context determines significance.  Scale teaches that size only matters in comparison.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Scale Shifting - Zoom In and Out.

Here's your activity: Take something that concerns you and view it at different scales: zoom in (what are the immediate details?) and zoom out (how does this look in 10 years? From someone else's life? Cosmically?). Different scales reveal different truths. This helps you practice viewing issues at different scales.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about big and small are relative can be applied to scale shifting - zoom in and out. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
